identitySignals: Name matches a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit: 'Unamesa Association' (ProPublica Nonprofit Explorer, EIN 20-5643483, Palo Alto, CA)

UnaMesa's own website says InPlay was launched in 2015 as its project to connect students to out-of-school learning, matching the agenda's 'UnaMesa Association dba InPlay' and OUSD's after-school and summer program contracts
InPlay's website names Oakland Unified School District as a partner for summer programs, matching OUSD's Community Schools and Student Services contracts
Registry city (Palo Alto) differs from the agenda's San Mateo, CA but is on the same Peninsula and the dba name matches exactly
research.notes: Agenda gives San Mateo, CA; ProPublica and UnaMesa's site give Palo Alto. Street address deliberately omitted because of that discrepancy. InPlay launched as an independent nonprofit in 2024 (separate entity, Inplay Learning Network); the OUSD contracts are 2020-2024 under UnaMesa Association dba InPlay, so the UnaMesa record is the right match.

profile.summary: UnaMesa Association is a nonprofit (501(c)(3)) charity that supports social entrepreneurs working on healthcare, education and social services. In 2015 it launched InPlay, a platform that connects students and families to summer and after-school programs. InPlay also provides registration and program-management tools for school districts, and became its own independent nonprofit in 2024.

review.notes: ProPublica confirms UnaMesa Association (EIN 20-5643483, 501(c)(3), Palo Alto); unamesa.org describes the 2015 InPlay launch and its 2024 independence, and inplay.org names Oakland USD as a partner and describes the summer/after-school registration tools. The dba name matches the agenda exactly; the San Mateo vs Palo Alto difference is minor and the address was omitted. The summary is supported and neutral.
